These are great diapers! I have been using them with my second child for about 6 weeks now and we have not had a single leak, which is pretty amazing! I ordered more recently to replace leaking diapers from my first child (not Nora's nursery brand). I have used a variety of pocket diapers including Alva's, wegreeco, and some other knock-off brands, and these are definitely the best! I also feel that they make a concerted effort to use sustainable sources, and I love that they come in a bag made of plant-based material. The covers are the exact same shape/snap placement as Alva diapers, but they are, in my opinion, much cuter! The inserts are also drastically superior to the microfiber inserts that come with most Alva diapers. I do I think they are comparable to the charcoal and bamboo inserts that Alva sells, but if you are going to buy the Alva diapers with the separate inserts, it's going to be about the same cost as the Nora's nursery diapers and since they are so much cuter, in my opinion, it's worth it to buy the ones I really like!one of the great things about cloth diapers is that they last for the entire time you are diapering your child, so I think it's worth getting ones that you really like! Regardless, you are going to be spending a lot less on these than you would on disposables or some of the extremely expensive cloth diapers. I do recommend doubling up inserts at night, I add a hemp insert in addition to a bamboo one. Also, it is critical that you correctly prep diapers before using them!

I was between this and the Jeep Overland Sport and I find this to be the more sturdy of the two and having the swivel wheel is just such a huge benefit. I have only 2 things of note. When walking at a brisk pace you need to make sure the front wheel is in the locked position, otherwise it will wobble on you. This being our first jogging stroller it is sort of a learning experience for us and I didn't think about this. Second, there are decorative caps that cover the front axle, and when you bind the quick release it compresses the plastic caps into the wheel hub. This makes the front wheel not spin 100% freely. I didn't find this to be a problem per se, but it made me wonder if I had installed the wheel correctly or not and wondered if they were supposed to be there or if they were supposed to be removed since the instructions and the photos on Amazon did not show them on the product. Otherwise it is just a fantastic stroller that my daughter seems to really enjoy to ride around in and I highly recommend it.

We have been using this monitor for 7 months now, with no problems. The clarity of the screen is very good, and ability to move the camera via the lcd screen is excellent. The night vision works great, as well as the volume control. It is nice to see the led's on the screen, range from green, to red, when our baby is really crying loud. It's just nice to have the ability to quickly turn on the screen, check on the baby, instead of physically getting up, and walking in the baby's room, potentially waking him up.

The range is also very good. Our baby can be sleeping in an upstairs room, all the way down the hall, and we can be 2 floors down, on the opposite end of the house, and still have signal. Also, the mic feature works well. If I go get the baby upstairs, my wife can talk to me on the mic, if she wants me to bring anything down from the baby's room. As far as signal quality goes; we have wifi constantly running, with 3 computers, and a smart phone, and their is no distortion or cross talk between any of the electronic devices and monitor.

The kickstand behind the monitor is great for propping up the monitor on an end table, while you do your thing around the house. Another nice addition, is the ability to add other monitors to the set up. We will be doing this shortly. We love this monitor and screen so much, that we convinced 3 other people in our family to purchase the set up.

With my first son, I had a Boppy nursing pillow. I used it for a few days after birth, and then I stopped using it. It wasn't at a correct angle for me,and I ended up supporting the baby with my arms anyway. I ordered this pillow initially because I thought if I didn't use it much for nursing, the toy feature would make it useful later on. With so many baby items that get limited use, it is great when anything as multiple uses. I loved this pillow more than I thought I would. The fabric is easy to wipe clean, and removes with a zipper for washing. The toy bar comes off completely with velcro, or it can lay flat against the sides of the pillow. I liked to put it along the sides of the pillow for tummy time. The toys that come with it are ok, but you can also attach other toys using  any standard rings, so you can switch out the toys when baby gets bored with what is there. For nursing, I loved that there were different sizes on each side. It does require that you flip the pillow when you change sides when nursing. Most of the time, my son only feeds on one side per feeding, so it isn't a big deal for me. The pillow doesn't lose its shape like the Bobby tends to. If you have time, you can soak up several prunes in just enough hot water until soft, blend it in your blender. Add water or prune/pear/apple juice for a thinner consistency. Put it in a squeezable pouch or drink it from a cup with straw!

I have been using this car seat for over 2.5 years and still recommend it to anyone who asks. We got one for my oldest when he was about 9 months old and used it rear facing for about 1 year and he's been forward facing now for about 1.5 years. My youngest also has the same seat. It is important that you find out if a car seat will work with your vehicle before purchasing. Many stores that sell them will let you take a model to your car to make sure it fits. That is what we did. People kept recommending that we get a Britax, but they just didn't fit right in our vehicle (Jeep Patriot). The Evenflo fit the bill for us. Below are my pros and cons.

Pros:
- We love the knobs for tightening and loosening the straps. First, they make it so easy to get a nice, snug fit with the straps. Since the knobs are on both sides it is still easy to use in both rear and forward facing positions. Also, the kids cannot reach them so there is no chance of them being able to loosen the straps themselves.
- Not having to rethread the straps every few months is great! You just firmly grasp near the shoulders and push the straps up or down. There are also more positions making sure you get a great, safe fit.
- The LATCH system works great with our vehicle. We do need to use a rolled up towel to get a good fit when in the rear facing position, but I hear that is not uncommon with many seats.

Cons:
- The cup holder that comes with the seat is flimsy and we discarded them early on. However, we have never really missed not having them.
- They are fairly wide seats and with two in our back seat, not adult can fit back there. We also are not sure if they would fit on a plane so we bought a Cosco Scenera for traveling.

In the forward facing position, sometimes my sons head does bob forward when he falls asleep. I am not sure if that is a by product of the seat though because sometimes he just rests his head on the side of the seat. We have been fortunate enough to never be involved in an accident, however, Consumer Reports gives it the highest rating for crash protection. This seat has been very good for us and would purchase it again.

I really appreciate the lenient return time because we had it sitting in our garage for a couple months. We returned it and got a FULL REFUND. Some products you return on amazon charge you some money to return if it's not defective. I commented that there was no problem, it was just no longer needed, and I wasn't penalized for it. Amazing customer service, very appreciated.

The main thing I've come to realize about sleep swaddles is that what works for one person may not work for another. You have to see what your baby takes to, and all babies are different! My baby was a big fan of halo sleepsacks! Comparing across the brand, I liked the cotton one over the microfleece because I preferred to have my son in jammies. Jammies+microfleece was just too hot.
Generally, what I like about halo sleepsacks is:
(1) The velcro is easy to secure / the wrap is easy to do
(2) You can go looser to let baby have some movement or get his arms out
(3) You can wrap it under baby's armpits to allow arms out totally
(4) The zipper at the bottom allows for diaper changes without unswaddling - so handy!
(5) The sizing seemed good, my son had plenty of room horizontally and vertically to stretch when he wanted while also feeling comfortably secure.

We tried a woombie and a swaddleme and the halo won out because it worked for my baby. Find what works for yours! If your baby has a startle reflex and likes being tightly wrapped, this is definitely worth a shot :)

I received this as a Baby Shower gift, purchased from my registry and I've been using it for approximately 6.5 weeks now. I really enjoy the pump. It is lightweight and easy to use. It automatically shuts off after 30 minutes which I think is a good feature in case someone would fall asleep while pumping. Also, from what I've found, most women don't need to pump more than 30 minutes at a time. However, since it remembers your last settings, even if you do want to or need to pump longer, you would be able to turn it right back on very quickly. Mine also came with the pumping accessories including 2 sets (sizes) of flanges. I have found it very easy to find replacement parts (looking for different sizes flanges - nothing wrong with the materials sent).

The cons: I wish there were different settings for each breast as sometimes one nipple seems able to withstand/need a little more suction than the other one. I also wish there was a way to wear this. I use a hands-free pumping bra but am limited to the space that the tubing allows me to go from the pump - which isn't very far, less than 2 feet. I'm sure some people could get creative and make something to carry/wear this since it is so lightweight though.

This is a great carrier and the price is unbeatable. The baby looks so cute looking up at me. He breathes rapidly (almost hyperventilating) when he gets excited about different things. He always hyperventilates when he is in this carrier.

There are some cons not exclusive to this carrier. As with all carriers of this type, if he goes to the bathroom, it can be uncomfortable because his whole body weight is pushing down on that diaper area. As a result, I've found that he has a lot of fun in the carrier, wets himself because of all the excitement, then has to be taken out of the carrier because of the discomfort of his body being supported right on top of a dirty diaper. Needless to say, this isn't a carrier for extended wear. As other reviewers have stated, the straps are not perfect either. So even if your baby can control their excitement, your back probably wouldn't be able to.

Never-the-less, I am giving this product five stars for the following reasons... First, Infantino has appropriately designed the carrier to be used by both male and female parents. (Some) Men like to care for their babies and it is unfair for decent men to have to deal with flowers and cartoon characters on everything; the black and white bib in the pictures can be completely removed on the carrier and what is left is a solid black, neutral design. There is no shame for men wearing this. Secondly, the baby loves being in it and I feel that he is completely safe and secure while hanging there. Lastly, even though I have only been able to get about 20 minutes per use out of this, the price more than makes up for it; we've paid $40-$60 on items for the baby that we have not used at all, so $15 for a product that both the baby and I like is completely reasonable.

Ultimately, my issues are more about the baby constantly using the diaper when in the carrier. The carrier itself is great. The only SLIGHT issue I had was that some of the secondary support straps on the back would occasionally slide, making the baby hang lower than I had originally adjusted for; this can be corrected by simply pulling up the shoulder straps or pulling down on the back straps.

I initially purchased the twenty dollar Homedics model from Bed Bath & Beyond because my pregnant wife has increasingly started snoring louder due to her pregnancy. But the Homedics model had some kind of short in it and would occasionally blare static abruptly and without warning. So I tried out the Graco Sweet Slumber. Yes, it's a big plastic egg with 7 buttons, but it's more than functional in it's simplicity.

One user said that the plug comes out of the front, but it actually comes out of the back side (below the 5 buttons). The front of the machine has two buttons (power and 60-minute timer). The unit CAN run on 4 AA batteries if you need it to, which is a nice feature.

Anyway, I also see how some may not like the unit because it's not loud enough. In a home that has a lot of noise outside, it would likely not be loud enough. But I just need to drown out my wife. I put the unit on the floor on my side of the bed, and at the second from the highest level, the unit was enough for me to sleep peacefully as my wife snored peacefully. So I think that I'm going to keep this one in our room for a while... In fact, I may have to buy a new one for our baby when she comes in April.

I knew I wanted to breastfeed from the moment I got pregnant. But I also knew that I would be working and I would need a breast pump to express milk when Willow was unable to nurse because I was at work. But, since Willow never latched on, I was glad that I had spent the money and bought what I feel is the best breast pump out there, the Medela Pump In Style Breast Pump.

The great thing about this breast pump is that it has two nozzles so you can express from both breasts at once, if you care to. It has a variable control so you can decide how much suction you would like to have. When I first started, I went with what it felt like when Willow tried to nurse and then as I used it, I was able to up the suction until I had it maxed out. And let me tell you. I know everyone is different, but when I really got into the pumping groove, I pumped an ounce a minute.

I just can't say enough good things about this pump. It's easy to use and has a handy shoulder bag to carry it in and comes with a freezer pack to store the milk. Everything a pumping mom needs!
